lines: THOUSANDS OF STANDS · ALL MUST GO
Runaway-order overstock, never stood on by armor. Buy one, get forty free. Delivery by hauler, who is also free, because he is a stand.
Every dwarf a king for one sitting. Surplus from a work order nobody remembers placing. Cushions sold separately. Crowns not included.
WE HAVE SEEN MEAT. WE CAN PROVE IT
Each cut certified by three witnesses and one confused butcher. For forts that have gone so long without, they've forgotten the word.
DRINK IS NEAR YOU. LOOK DOWN
The barrel is beside you. It has been beside you the whole time. Please lift it. A public service for dwarves who die politely of thirst.
FOR DWARVES WHO WORK BESIDE GEMS
A mug strapped to your rough gems, for carpenters who would otherwise expire next to a heap of them. Gems not drinkable. We checked.
Our burrows are not thirty levels down. Forgotten beasts are politely asked to use the other stairs. There are no other stairs.
SAFETY, BUT CLOSER TO THE EXIT
Why hide thirty levels down when you could hide one level down, near a door, with a lever? Ask about our beast-facing reviews.
THE PIT TAKES. THE PIT KEEPS
Our haulers carry refuse INTO the pit, never back out of it, and never while it is raining rubbish. We learned. Training was costly.
For miners who climb up and simply stay. Our ladders reach the ground, which is where the drinks are. Trees not endorsed.
Bonsai lodging for dwarves who want the outdoors but would like to survive it. All branches at knee level. Ale at ankle level.
THOUSANDS OF JOBS, ONE DAY AT A TIME
Weekly meetings in an unsmoothed room, which we are not allowed to smooth. Please stop touching the walls. Please.
WE KEEP ONE UNCUT. FOR EMERGENCIES
When the mood strikes and every gem has been polished, break glass. Glass not cut either. Ask the gem-cutter to look away.
BUY ROUGH. HOLD ROUGH. NEVER CUT
Our analysts predict the next mood will ask for exactly what the fort just finished cutting. They are never wrong. Sell your wheel.
WHEN YOUR CHILD DEMANDS PLANT CLOTH
We keep a bolt on hand for every tiny genius. Crayons, blocks, one loom. Kids leave with an artifact and a nap.
When the possession comes and the workshop is still a sketch, our loom-on-wheels comes to you. Carts may knock. Weavers may shriek.
SEVEN SCRAPS IS NOT A STOCKPILE
We count your cloth properly, so a few rags never again convince the management the fort is drowning in fabric. Rates in thread.
HOSPITALS WITH A DWARF IN THEM
Unlike certain wards we could name, every bed comes with a doctor, or at least a dwarf holding a splint confidently.
Wave a lost fort's artifact about like a hero. Weight and glory approximate. Not an artifact; please do not let a noble name it.
SEE THE OLD FORT. FROM A HILL
It is still there. So are the goblins who live in it now. Telescope included, courage not. Tours leave weekly, return occasionally.
Read how {past_fort} {past_fort_fate} in its original typeface. All {past_fort_years}. Bring a candle and a strong stomach.
The monarch has never held one, but has walked near our kiosk. Printed with a crown, which is close enough for the provinces.
A trading house in the liaison's own style. We recommend import agreements. We then recommend more. Rings at any markup you like.
We asked {liaison} what rings are worth. The answer was a percentage. Of what, nobody said. Order now while percents last.
For every polite table in {world}. Plus two blank cards for the goblins, who do not read cards and eat the blank ones.
Full cover against total war, partial cover against skirmishes, no cover against your beard falling out from the stress of it.
NOT A TOTAL WAR? NOT A TOTAL HELMET
Our half-helms protect the half of your head goblins usually aim at. The other half is your problem and your beard's.
Every town that fell to a goblin army had ordinary doors. You don't have to. Install by midwinter. Fitting crew flees on request.
Bedrolls, one hot mug and a map that does not include any goblin armies. Serving every band of the displaced since the last army marched.
We sell fish. We have never besieged a town. Please stop sending us angry letters addressed to goblin warlords with similar names.
FROM A TOWN OF CAKE PEOPLE
Light, fluffy, fragile. Most arrive as crumbs. The crumbs are exquisite. Dwarves eat the box too.
IT WAS OURS. IT IS OURS AGAIN
We reclaim lost halls, sweep out the bones and leave a small plaque that says 'mine'. {past_fort} is on our list.
Non-slip soles for marching into a fortress the goblins are still using. Grip on blood, ichor, ale and goblin. Smell stays forever.
Probably not. Subscribe anyway and receive a weekly bell telling you it is still somewhere else. On the bad week, the bell is silent.
KEEP GIANT BEASTS OUT OF SIGHT
Heavy curtains for those who live near a crooked horror and would rather not wake to one. Do not peek. It peeks back.
Our bells ring when anyone is snatched. Elves have used them twice. Both times the bell was also snatched.
IS IT YOUR GREAVES? JOIN THE QUEUE
Forty-odd figures claim the same lost artifact. You could be next. It sits in a far fort, wanted by all, amused by none.
So does everyone. Getting it back is a separate service, with a separate price, and a separate will for you to sign.
WHEN THE GODS BLINK, WE PAY
Coverage for anything lost when the world stops and starts: half a tunnel, a fresh mood, the meal you thought you ate. Claims paid twice.
Feeling you have dug this tunnel before? You have. Our counsellors explain the Great Rewinds gently, then again, then again.
Speak with the ghosts of {past_fort}. Mostly they ask for a drink. They were sitting next to plenty. They know. Ask anyway.
UNIFORMS FOR TEN, WORN BY ONE
Our captain bundles: one full kit and nine empty hangers that salute when you walk by. Guaranteed 'Off duty' lustre.
Comfortable, padded and permanently relaxed. As worn by militias of one. Matching slippers for nine more feet.
Pre-filled, pre-stamped and pre-filed by the mayor's office. Just add a dwarf's name. Any dwarf. The mayor isn't fussy.
STAND IN THE PUMPS. FEEL HAPPY
Pumped spray, windmill-powered, guaranteed fine mist and one happy thought. Do not drink the mist. Actually, do drink something.
Keeping the fort's windmills spinning with our signature hand-blown breeze. Six dwarves, one bellows, endless lungs.
We store it beautifully. Whether anyone drinks it is not our department. Thirsty miners are referred to the Bureau of Paradox.
Plenty of room in the catacombs since the last 'Safety' drill. Tasteful slabs, engraved quietly. Ghosts may lodge complaints.
A tall tower with an excellent view and a short history of being used. Gift shop at the base. The top floor is for staff.
THE OVERSEER IS WATCHING. LOOK NICE
The Overseer's eye roams the halls and follows guests about. Our oil keeps you shiny when it swoops in. Glare-free.
THE WHOLE MAP. IN THE RAIN
The Overseer wants every plant from every corner of the map. Today. In the rain. Our coats are waterproof; the plants are not.
A whole wing dedicated to the fort's most famous number. Guided tours, souvenir plaques, one curator who still cannot explain it.
Our advisors were there. Hire us before your next work order and we'll stand behind the manager whispering the figure, gently.
Still thirsty? Call us. We walk over, hand you a mug and watch you drink it. Our record: a miner found beside two thousand of them. Sadly.
WE WALK YOU TO THE BARREL
A trained companion for any dwarf who has forgotten where the {drinks} drinks are. Fee: one sip. Hand-holding optional.
The last fort had 800. You have more. We help forts accept that a stone can just be left where it fell. Group hugs, with the stones.
FOR FORTS OF {dogs} DOGS OR MORE
The old fort kept thirteen and still felt lonely. Bunk kennels, chew-proof doors, a bone in every bowl. Cats sneer at our prices.
We understand. One old fort tilled twenty and ate plump helmets for half a decade. Try our Pretend Steak, carved from a mushroom.
Rent a rough gem for your next mood. Return it carved into an artifact. Late fees apply if the artifact is a cage.
Whatever the mood demands, we have one. We especially have the thing you just used up. That is our whole business model.
A mug engraved with the departed's name, filled with drink, so this time no one is far from one. Proceeds to the Thirst Fund.
If the Overseer melts it, sells it or forgets it on a stockpile at the map's edge, we pay out. In plump helmets, mostly.
On becoming {post}. Our classes teach the newly titled how to sit in an office, sign forms and look busy near the mayor.
And the Overseer has ordered two thousand things out of it. We teach restraint. Final exam: carve one thing. Then stop. Then stop again.
Before anyone queues a hundred and fifty thrones, please speak to our advisors, who will hide the logs somewhere sensible, like a tree.
Some forts start with none. We count every roast, every biscuit and every dwarf near one, so the famine stays a story.
Every seed locked away from dwarves who plant one and eat four. A handful of plants once fed ten dwarves. Never again, we hope.
Before your bars become armor stands, consider literally anything else. We buy metal, sell metal, and never queue furniture.
Our counters number your livestock every season, then again after the Great Rewind, to be safe. Surprisingly often it differs.
We give every cat a bed, a stockpile to sit on and an owner it ignores. Expansion planned if the cats approve, which they won't.
For the fort's most numerous creature. Meetings in the pasture. Members are mostly the animals. Minutes taken by the dogs.
Real numbers, not seven scraps. Our weavers will tell you the truth before any mood, possession or loom-room queue does.
The Overseer has blocks. We have ideas for them other than smoothing, stands or thrones. Ask about our walls. Just walls.
Mediation for crowded halls. Founded by survivors of the great dining-hall queue. Bring a mug and a grievance, in that order.
{past_fort} began with even less. You are doing better. Probably. Join our circle and count each other twice.
Our almanac predicts the season's runaway order. Last forecast: thrones. Correct. We were also correct about the stands.
Whatever it is, the Overseer will send someone out to gather plants in it. Our capes protect against most weather and some goblins.
YET ANOTHER FORT, YET ANOTHER YEAR
Plates for every fort of the line, past, present and whoever is next. Plates stack. So do forts.
EVERY FORT WE EVER LOST, MAPPED
Pinpoint the goblin-run ruins, the thrones and the trees we no longer climb. Fully indexed by cause of thirst.
Our spokesdwarf {citizen} has drunk one every single day and says it is the secret to staying alive near a drink stockpile.
NOT A 'SAFETY' BURROW. A NAP ONE
Strictly one level down from the dining hall, near a drink and far from any staircase a beast might enjoy. Book a slot today.
We knock, you drink. If you are up a tree, we wait below with a mug and a ladder. If you are in the garbage pit, please come out.
Commissions now open, except for armor stands, thrones and anything else that might accidentally be ordered two thousand times.
Join others who have walked past the artifact and felt something. Monthly viewing. Do not touch. Do not mood near it.
MOVING ON? WE PACK THE GHOSTS
Experienced in relocating whole civilizations from one doomed fort to the next. We have done this three times this decade alone.
Help restore the first fort, currently being restored by The Torments of Hating into something with more spikes.
Counselling for groups recently pushed out of a fort by goblins, humans, or both. Shared waiting room with The Distinct Dungeon.
Proud locksmiths to whoever currently occupies Jackaldefense. At present, The Grooved Council. Keys cut while you are evicted.
The Glowing Cult, The Wayward Doctrine, The Deified Lantern and The Distant Letter all trust us. Each with a different leader.
WE ROLL WHERE THE HEX DOESN'T
Overland freight from Crazeboard, Massivebarbs and Toeembrace. Routes avoid Padtufted, goblins and the past.
Imported from the elf retreat. We removed the leaves and added ale. Elves call it an outrage. Dwarves call it tea.
Flower bulbs from Bulbwhisker. Will grow into a tree. Tree will grow into a problem. Problem will cost you a caravan.
Rope, rations, a note reading 'I am very bony.' Tested by snatchers outside Seducedbowl, Menacetested and Quietmenaces.
A public warning from the Herald Board of Place Names. Do not trust any dark fortress to be what it says. Menacetested is also menacing.
Our three products, made in amounts only the Overseer could love. Bulk discounts begin at one thousand. Nothing smaller sold.
A mechanical stop for runaway work orders. Pull the lever and the 1,982nd armor stand never happens. Patent pending since Quakefocus.
Second-hand strategies: one cistern-first approach, one 'smooth it all' plan, one bravely starving founding. Some wear.
Quakefocus survived it, so we celebrate it, with one plump helmet shared between ten dwarves for authenticity. Bring a spoon.
FEED TEN DWARVES ON A HANDFUL
The Starving Founding Plan. Results: dramatic. Testimonials: few. Free consultation, no meals provided, as per the plan.
Fey, secretive, possessed, fell or macabre, we cover them all, except for dying of thirst. Nobody will insure that around here.
NO TREE, NO BRANCH, NO PROBLEM
After the branch incident we offer a full tree extraction. Elves are not to be informed. Please keep the caravans indoors.
PUMPING MIST SINCE THE RING WENT IN
Our members pump so you can stand in a gentle spray and feel nice. Ask about the job openings. There are always openings.
Mobile medical service for any hospital left without a healer. We bring splints, thread and a firm handshake.
The post sits empty again. We introduce suitable dwarves to the hospital. Most run. The fastest are offered the job.
A FRIEND FOR THE MILITIA OF ONE
Lonely captain? Nine empty places? We provide cardboard squadmates with excellent posture. They also refuse to train.
DRINK HERE. YOU'RE IN THE MILITIA
Our barrel conscripts anyone who touches it. Note: as of press time nobody has touched it. The captain drinks from the well.
The mayor's office has worn through eleven stamps this season. Ours last longer. Ink in red, redder and furious.
Mayor, sheriff, hammerer, dungeon master, champion and doctor: their chairs are ready. Their occupants are not. Dust included.
For the fort's next hammerer, whoever that may be. Not yet appointed. Pillow may be appointed instead.
A WHIP, A KEY, NO APPLICANTS
Everything the dungeon master needs, should one ever arrive. Currently displayed in our window, collecting a fine dust.
Our trophies honour the champion, a post that has stayed vacant so long the trophy has started to feel like the champion.
THE PIT IS ONE-WAY. BE ONE-WAY TOO
Signs, arrows and a firm dwarf with a whistle to stop haulers fetching rubbish back out while more is tipped onto their heads.
A bell on every flight between the fort and its deepest burrow. If something big climbs the stairs, you'll hear it in time.
Lot 1: a {past_fort} tankard (full). Lot 2: a throne (one of very many). Lot 3: a branch (do not climb).
Dwarven cheese aged in the gap between the gods blinking. Tastes of yesterday. Possibly literally. Sold in wheels, twice.
Bring your list. We add rings. We remove your list. A humble liaison's service, handled with much to share and nothing to show.
A private hall for citizens of The Chambers of Steel. Steel chairs, steel tables, steel mugs. The ale is, thankfully, ale.
Sixteen baskets for sixteen friendly groups. Two smaller baskets, mostly rocks, for the goblins we are fighting.
FOR TOTAL WARS OF ALL SIZES
Tables, flags and little goblin figurines labelled 'The Destined Wickedness'. Flags available in 'surrender' at no extra cost.
Or Imara Sidayanithe? Neither has their retreat. We look in towers, cages and the backs of goblin wagons.
WOVEN BY THE SILKS OF CREMATING
Genuine cloth from the refugee band of the same name. Strong, warm, unsettling label. Proceeds to rebuilding Ironcrowds.
The Society of Creeds and The Society of Adoration, combined for one night. Songs about fleeing. Very hummable.
WE FIX WHAT THE HEX BROKE
Plumbers from the old town of Pulledrained, now at large. We fix wells, cisterns and mist rings. Paid in sympathy and ale.
Our motto is 'nearby'. We dig modest rooms close to everything you need, including water, doors and the exits. Revolutionary.
YOU POLISHED THEM ALL. NOW WHAT?
Counselling for jewellers who cut every last gem, only for three moods in a row to ask for a rough one. It is not your fault.
Policies for parents whose infant may seize a workshop. Covers plant cloth, bone and one crayon artifact per child.
Safe railings above the refuse pit for dwarves who just want to see the rubbish without bringing it back up. Tickets: one sock.
Stroll past the pumps and receive one free happy thought. Second happy thought for a small fee. Third requires a nap.
We have carved 'Searabbeys', 'Quakefocus' and 'Creaturemirrored'. We keep a blank slab ready, just in case.
Bound volumes of the Creaturemirrored Pickaxe & Tribune, the Quakefocus Sentinel and whatever Searabbeys wrote on walls.
Our resident comic tells the same joke to each armor stand individually. Show runs nineteen years. Reserve now.
WHY STAND WHEN YOU CAN RULE?
Every dwarf deserves a throne at the dining table. We have 148 to lend. The nobles have complained. They were on thrones.
In honour of a Searabbeys miner found dehydrated beside 1,994 drinks. Donations buy mugs that hang around every miner's neck.
A sanctuary for the last uncut stones of the fort. Visit, adopt, protect. Moody dwarves may apply under supervision.
Like the Overseer's eye, we trail merchants, diplomats and animal people around the halls. Unlike it, we carry snacks.
Hats with ear-holes, chairs with tail-holes, mugs for snouts. Our depot lounges welcome all who walk upright, mostly.
Is a goblin army coming this {season}? We say yes. We always say yes. One day we will be right, and we will be insufferable.
AS FLED BY THE PLAIN FELLOWSHIP
Lightweight bedrolls, a fast pair of boots and a pocket map showing everywhere The Crazed Hex has not been. Map is small.
LUNCH FOR TEN, EATEN BY ONE
Our militia lunch packs are portioned for a full squad. The captain has never complained. He is very full.
We give visiting merchants a drink before they ask, unlike some miners we could mention. Elves receive water, sulkily.
THE MAP IS WHITE. GO ANYWAY
The Overseer still wants plants in the snow. We sell mittens and a small shovel. Plants are under there somewhere.
Clear skies mean the Overseer will send you to every corner of the map for herbs. Our hats have brims. The map has no shade.
Every spring the queue refreshes. So do our chisels. Buy one, smooth one, discover there are 9,999 left.
Our summer reminder: drinks are in the stockpile, not up a tree. Free reminder bells for miners. Ring them near barrels.
Our clerks recount the harvest to be sure it beat {past_fort}'s worst year. So far, every autumn, it has been. Barely.
Goblins love winter. So does cold. Our wool socks hold up to both. Left socks guaranteed; right socks, inquire.
Founded by dwarves, renovated by The Torments of Hating. New spikes in every hall. The Nuanced Hamlet viewable through a gap.
A full day of furniture. Lunch served on a throne, beside a stand, near more stands. Gift shop sells, guess what, stands.
The Crazed Hex came. The Vice of Fins came. We come next, with bricks. Volunteers welcome, goblins not.
Rooms with a view of a crooked horror. Discount if it is home. Large discount if it is hungry. Refund if you are eaten.
Join 48 rival claimants on a coach trip. Fistfights at every stop. The greaves remain where they are, amused.
Our travel desk has never sent a single dwarf there and never will. We just think the name is a lesson. Read it twice.
Searabbeys, Quakefocus, Creaturemirrored: one occupied, one abandoned, one ours. Pack a lot of drink. Actually drink it this time.
Tour the halls Bomrek Thimshursåkzul won back. Floors scrubbed, bones stacked, ghosts asked to wait outside.
It {past_fort_fate}. Now the halls have new tenants, new spikes and a strict no-dwarves policy. Viewings from the ridge only.
See where it all went right, then wrong, then very wrong. Guide points at each spot and says 'here'. Lunch is a single mushroom.
Coach trip to the site of the world's most explainable-in-hindsight number. Gift shop sells one of each. Thankfully only one.
Weekly carts across the realm. Routes reviewed by the liaison, who recommends an import agreement at every single stop.
Updated each season with the last known position of every goblin host. Three towns found out the hard way. We printed late.
The goblins came, the goblins went, we come next with bricks. Volunteers welcome, goblins not, unless they carry bricks.
A gathering for everyone who fled. Bring your fellowship, your society and whatever you managed to carry out at a run.
Visit the humans. Eat a cake. Eat their cake. Leave with crumbs in your beard and an import agreement in your pocket.
Whoever took it this year welcomes you to a town recently home to someone else. Previous tenants are not on the tour.
Tour the halls our cousins won back. Floors scrubbed, bones stacked, ghosts asked politely to wait outside for a bit.
Our cousins are in there now. Things are going about as well as expected. Visitors are asked to bring a weapon and a mop.
Lodgings overlooking a giant beast's lair. Discount if it is home. Large discount if it is hungry. Refund if you are eaten.
Quiet, dark and lightly haunted by something large. Lights out at dusk. It comes out at dusk too. Shared schedule.
Join every rival claimant of a famous lost artifact on one coach. Fistfights at every stop. The artifact stays put, amused.
WE GO WHERE THEY WERE TAKEN
Elves abducted from groves all over {world}. We look in towers, cages and the backs of goblin wagons. Success rate: pending.
A night at a real dark fortress, run by goblins oddly fond of tourists. Ticket price includes the rescue party.
Send a card from a goblin tower. Ours come pre-stained so no one can tell whether it was the ink or something worse.
Our carts are carved from stone to avoid offending elves. They weigh nine tonnes and travel very, very slowly.
Elven hospitality: sing, sway, eat a leaf. Do not mention the thrones. The elves heard about the hundreds of wooden thrones.
A quiet hamlet with three houses, two pigs and one tavern that has never heard of armor stands. Book before it does.
A DAY, A MUG, A WAVE
We take you there, you have one drink, you wave at a farmer, we bring you home. Bestselling for three forts running.
Annual market. A human sells planks to dwarves whose fort has a hundred thrones of planks. Somehow he always sells out.
Founded by bands with names like 'The Silks' and 'The Society'. Our carts never stop, because whoever is behind us never stops.
Leaders change fast in {world}. Cults, doctrines, lanterns: all under new management by Thursday. Our weekly keeps track.
Line the road as the ruler of {civ} passes by, probably, at some point. Bring a chair. Your fort has hundreds.
The liaison's favourite inn between {town} and {fort}. Breakfast includes a long talk on import agreements and rings.
Where are the enemy armies? Wherever the map is rolled up. Laminated in slate for use under arrows.
Mountains, goblin towers, elf groves and at least one crooked horror. Hatch opens briefly. Closes quickly. Screams optional.
Like many an old dwarf fort, it was once someone's home. Now it has spikes, pits and a doormat that bites. Viewings by force.
If the world stops and restarts mid-journey, we honour your ticket twice. Your luggage may arrive yesterday.
Not by goblins, not by humans, not recently. Come before that changes. Bring a cart that turns quickly.
See the capital. Meet a clerk. Be recommended an import agreement in person. Return with rings at a very specific markup.

classifieds.text: Armor stand. Lightly unused. One of several thousand. Will also accept offers for the others, which are standing behind it, menacingly.
Throne, oak, never sat on by a noble. Nobles had their pick of a hundred and chose the floor out of spite.
Will swap one throne for one meal. Two thrones for two meals. Have a lot of thrones. Am very hungry.
Armor stands. Free to good home. Free to bad home. Free to any home. Please. They are blocking the stairs.
My way back up from the 'Safety' burrow. Thirty levels of stairs and something large on them. Reward if found, or if you find the stairs.
Ladder, tall, sturdy. To fetch a friend off a branch. Urgency high. Tree does not seem bothered either way.
To whoever keeps dumping refuse into the pit while I am down there fetching it back out: we need to talk. Loudly. From down here.
To my fellow haulers: I brought the rubbish back out of the pit because the Overseer said to. I now see why that was wrong.
One rough gem. Uncut, glorious, and immediately demanded by a fisherdwarf in a strange mood. Claim it if you are faster than him.
ROUGH GEM. Any colour. Do not cut it. Do not look at the cutter. Contact the butcher, who is having a mood and is not well.
To the gem cutter: you have cut every gem in the fort. Every one. We admire your work. Please put the wheel down for one season.
Plant cloth for a child. Not a costume. A strange mood. The child has taken a workshop and will not discuss bedtime.
The child in the clothier's shop is not playing. Do not tell her it is cute. She is making an artifact and has a schedule.
Our loom room. The weaver is waiting, possessed, and may not wait long. Last seen behind the smoothing queue, which is everything.
Seven silk scraps. They were the cloth stockpile, according to the Overseer, who has stopped ordering cloth because of them.
Seven silk scraps. Previously believed to be an entire cloth industry. Now merely scraps. Price reflects the drama.
For any dwarf who can explain how a carpenter dies of thirst beside a hundred rough gems. Reward is one rough gem, cut, sadly.
Personal drink reminders. I follow you, I point at the barrel, I say 'drink'. Clients include every miner in living memory. Most survived.
Will stand beside you holding a mug while you work. Strongly recommended for miners, carpenters and anyone near a pile of gems.
There are {drinks} drinks in the stockpile. We know. Please, please, please drink one. The Society for Not Repeating History.
Meat. Any meat. Veterans can describe it if you have never seen it. It is brown and you eat it. Fish also acceptable.
Commemorative 'Meat Watch' bell. Rang once, false alarm. It was a very brown mushroom.
Veteran of the meatless years seeks companion to stare at a roast with. Need not be eaten. Just looked at. Lovingly.
Eight hundred loose stones, old fort vintage. Swap for anything that is not a stone. Will consider other stones if very different.
Our old fortress, {past_fort}. It {past_fort_fate}. If found, please do not return it; it probably has spikes now.
Whoever lives in {past_fort} now has re-signed the lease. We were not consulted. The landlord was not consulted. The landlord is a goblin.
Volunteers to recover an artifact left behind at {past_fort}. Bring shields, nerve and no plans for later in the year.
Back issues of the old fort's paper. Includes the famous famine edition. Pages slightly chewed; we were very hungry.
A handful of plants. Must feed ten dwarves. Hopes high. Contact any surviving founder of {past_fort}. There are some. Mostly.
Smoothing. One dwarf, one chisel, ten thousand jobs. Current wait: forty years. Do not ask about the other two smoothers.
Unsmoothed room, rough walls, real character. Smoothers keep trying to sneak in at night. Lock provided, chisel-proof.
I smoothed your bedroom while you were asleep in it. It was on the list. Everything is on the list. I am sorry. I am also not stopping.
Doctors are needed in two of the four hospitals. Patients in those hospitals are advised to visit the other two, or heal by thinking.
Chief medical dwarf. Office empty. Whoever had it last left a splint on the desk and a note: 'gone looking for a doctor'.
A famous artifact mace. Not found exactly. Still at the old fort. But we know where it is, which counts for something.
Dear liaison: there is much to share, you say. Then share some. Of anything. Just once. Yours, everyone at the trade depot.
Rings, priced at whatever percent {liaison} requested. Selling them back at one percent more. The liaison may recommend this agreement.
The liaison has recommended another import agreement. Our import agreements now recommend their own import agreements.
Someone to tell {monarch} about the thrones. Gently. The monarch thinks we are building a palace. We are, kind of, a furniture one.
Letter-writing to our diplomat. Phrases for peace with sixteen groups and for 'please stop' with the other two.
For news of {enemy} that does not include the word 'coming'. Reward triples if it includes 'gone home'.
Skirmish only, say some goblins. Total war, say others. Both, says the militia captain, who is one dwarf.
Refugee, recently of a sacked town, seeks fellow refugee for walks, talks and running from goblin armies.
A boot belonging to a fleeing refugee society. The rest of the society was moving too quickly to collect it. Claim at gate.
Former neighbours from the town with the well. You know who you are. The goblins live there now. Let's meet for ale.
Shield, big enough to hide behind when the goblin warlord visits. Also big enough for a friend. And his goat.
The goblin generals are NOT invited to the solstice dinner. Neither knows. Keep it that way.
Silks woven by a refugee band with an unsettling name chosen by committee. Exquisite. Warm. Sold with a reassuring leaflet.
Compliments, one coin each. Discount for groups recently evicted from their fortress by goblins, humans, or both.
To the dwarves evicted from that town: sorry. We did not take it. The humans did. We just watched. Glad we didn't help.
Dwarf group seeks new home. Lost the old one to goblins, lost the leader to succession. Has kept the letterhead.
Old halls reclaimed nearby. All ghosts asked to move out by spring. Several ghosts say they were there first. They were.
Famous lost greaves, genuine. Seller is claimant #31. Buyer will be claimant #49. Greaves remain in a fort far away.
For return of a lost artifact to its rightful owner. Owners listed overleaf. And on the next leaf. And the next 46 leaves.
Applicants claiming the lost greaves form a queue at the back of the meeting hall. The queue goes out the door and has done for decades.
Brave dwarf to visit the crooked horror's lair and confirm it is still there. Confirmation from a distance is fine. Very fine.
Map of {world}, complete with the location of every goblin army. Map is mostly red. Sold at a discount for that reason.
Rewind recovery: if the gods blinked and you lost a day, I will tell you what you did. You dug a tunnel. You always dig a tunnel.
Yesterday. Gone in the Great Rewind. If you have it, it was the one where I almost finished my masterwork. Please return.
A day, extra. Appeared after the gods blinked. Already used it to dig the same tunnel again. Free to whoever wants the leftover.
Ghost of a thirsty miner seeks a drink. Was beside two thousand of them at the time and took none. Lesson learned, too late.
Ghosts from previous forts are reminded to haunt their OWN forts. {past_fort} is two valleys over. Please go there.
Exorcist with experience in ghosts who died of thirst. Must bring a mug. The ghosts mainly want a mug.
Spare bedroom, newly vacant after the 'Safety' burrow drill. Furniture intact, ghost polite. Do not take the stairs down.
One deep burrow, slightly haunted, thirty levels down. Will trade for any room on the ground floor, even a closet.
One branch. Removed from the tree for safety. Has a history. Do not climb it, even lying on the floor. Especially then.
To the tree: we know it was not your fault. To the miner: we know it was not yours either. We blame the Overseer, quietly.
Dwarves are reminded that a tree is not a workshop, nor a bedroom, nor a place to wait for a drink to arrive.
Searabbeys. Last seen under the management of The Torments of Hating. If found, please do not return it; it has spikes now.
Ghost of Bomrek, Searabbeys miner, seeks a drink. Was beside 1,994 drinks at the time. Did not take one. Embarrassed.
Back issues, Quakefocus Sentinel. Includes the famous 'famine, day 32' edition. Pages slightly chewed; we were very hungry.
Iden: there is much to share, you say. Then share some. Of anything. Just once. Yours, everyone at the trade depot.
Mame Ayathemiyi, taken at Nobledessert, and Imara Sidayanithe, at Keeperglossed. The elves wrote to us on bark. Nobody dared reply.
Claimants of The Amusing Duties: the queue starts at Roughnessslaps and ends at Fieryaged. Bring a snack. Bring forty-seven snacks.
Dwarf to count the armor stands. Must be good with numbers, very good with very large numbers, and fine with sleeping among stands.
Work order, slightly used. Set to 'one'. Somehow produced thousands. Selling before it does it again. Do not look at it directly.
The manager wishes to confirm that nobody ordered the thrones. The thrones wish to confirm that they are here anyway.
One work order, last seen running away. Answers to 'repeat'. If found, do not feed it bars.
Furniture removal. We haul surplus thrones and armor stands to the edge of the map, where the Overseer finds them and hauls them back.
Lonely armor stand seeks armor. Any armor. Will stand very still. Has had a lot of practice.
Will trade 300 armor stands for one suit of armor. Or for a room without armor stands. Either. Please.
To the dwarf I sat on a throne beside: there were no other chairs, only thrones. I am not a noble. I just wanted my soup.
Smoother's apprentice. You will smooth. You will smooth tomorrow. You will retire smoothing. The queue will remain.
The smoothing queue has achieved a length of its own and will now be referred to as 'the Queue', with a capital Q and a small office.
One unsmoothed wall, in a corner of the fort. Do not tell the Overseer. It is ours. We visit it and feel rough and free.
Three smoothers. Last seen entering the queue. Thought to be somewhere around job four thousand. Send biscuits.
A drink. I had it right in my hand and I put it down to finish a job. I died of thirst. This advert is placed by my ghost.
Thirst Watch. I follow miners through every tunnel ringing a bell and yelling 'MUG'. Hated by miners. Loved by their families.
If you feel thirsty, there are {drinks} drinks. If you still feel thirsty after that, you are a ghost. Please see the notice board for ghosts.
Anyone who can explain why the barrels are full and the miners are not. Contact the Bureau of Paradox, room unsmoothed, desk dusty.
Dwarf to escort {citizen} to the drink stockpile and back. {citizen} knows the way. {citizen} just doesn't go.
{citizen_first}: the barrel is right there. It loves you. It has always loved you. Pick it up. Signed, everyone.
Climbing instructor for trees. Specialising in climbing DOWN. Upward courses already over-subscribed, with tragic results.
My cousin. Last seen up a tree reaching for a branch that 'looked like it had a drink on it'. It did not. Send a ladder.
Trees are not to be climbed, hugged, fallen from, died in or sat in until a drink comes. Elves may hug them; elves are outside.
Burrow labelled 'Safety'. Very deep. Very private. Stairs come right to the door, which turned out to be the problem.
The 'Safety' burrow is being renamed 'Mostly Safety' after review. Signs are being repainted. The stairs remain stairs.
Someone to stand at the top of the stairs and look down every few minutes. Must have a loud voice and a good sense of 'big'.
To everyone in the deep burrow: we thought something coming up the stairs would knock first. It did not. We are so sorry.
Burrow appraisal. I will tell you, from the doorway, if your 'Safety' burrow is actually safe. Rates waived if it isn't. You'll need them.
Refuse goes DOWN the pit. Nobody goes down the pit to fetch it back UP. This is the entire policy. It is one sentence.
One bucket of rubbish, retrieved from the pit at great personal cost. Will trade for an apology from whoever kept tipping more in.
Sign painter for the refuse pit. 'ONE WAY' in large letters. Arrows. Perhaps a drawing of a dwarf saying 'no'.
For the haul job that sent eight dwarves back into the garbage pit. We wish only to talk to it. With hammers.
ROUGH gems. Yes, again. The new mood has asked for exactly what we cut last week. Every week, this is the advert.
From now on, one gem in every hundred will be left rough and hidden in a sock. Do not ask which sock. You know which sock.
To the strange mood that keeps asking for the one thing we just ran out of: we see you. We think you can see our stockpile.
One ugly rough gem in the refuse pile. Keep it safe. A mood will want it in about a week. It always does.
Spare workshop. A {moodname} is wandering the halls, muttering about bones, and has eyed my kitchen twice.
To {moodname}: we cut the last gem about ten minutes before your mood. Truly. We are as upset as you are. Almost.
Parents: if your child walks into a workshop with a far-off look, do not call them for dinner. Call the bookkeeper. Then hide the cloth.
Child's first artifact. A crown made of plant cloth, given a name longer than the child. Does not fit any head. Priceless.
One captain's worth of friends. The militia is one dwarf and nine empty places. He has been 'Off duty' so long he owns a rocking chair.
Militia drill this evening. The entire squad will attend. He has asked for a bigger room so it feels busier.
Militia captain, solo, seeks nine dwarves to stand behind him looking stern. No training required. No training occurs.
Nine unused militia uniforms. Folded, labelled, waiting. The captain irons them on Sundays.
The militia's enthusiasm. Last seen before it went 'Off duty'. Has not been back on since. Reward: one training session.
The mayor's office has filed a production order violation against the production order office. The case continues.
To the mayor: I did not make the mandated item because I was asleep. I am still asleep. My spouse filed this advert.
Lawyer, any species, to defend dwarves against production order violation charges. Paid in the item we were supposed to make.
I will make whatever the mayor demanded today, before the mayor demands it. Fee covers foresight, materials and nerves.
Positions still open: mayor, sheriff, hammerer, dungeon master, champion, chief medical dwarf. Applications to an empty desk.
Sheriff's badge. Never worn. Shiny. Office comes with it. Duties come with the office. Badge does not come with an applicant.
One hammerer's hammer, unused. Comes with a stern look and no hammerer. Excellent doorstop.
Mayor's office, available. Previous occupant took the chair. Next occupant: unknown. Desk drawer full of violation forms.
Mist ring maintenance. I keep the pumps spraying so you get a happy thought while walking past. Nobody thanks me, but they are happy.
Please walk through the mist ring slowly. The happy thought takes a moment to arrive. It is a very slow thought.
My hat, blown off by the windmill. Last seen heading north. Windmill has not admitted anything.
Somebody to drink from the cistern. It is full. It is lovely. Nobody visits. It is starting to feel unwanted.
The catacombs have reached capacity. Additional ghosts are asked to wait in the dining hall, quietly, not moving the cutlery.
Ghost, recently of a deep burrow, seeks other ghosts for a support group. Theme: stairs. We meet at the top of them.
Tour guide for the execution tower. Must explain it is mostly for the view. Must say it convincingly.
Guests: the Overseer's eye may follow you about the fort. It is only looking. Please wave. Please do not wave an axe.
One merchant, wandering the halls, followed by the Overseer's gaze. Claims he was looking for the depot. Claim him at the depot.
Herb gatherers. The whole map. In the rain. All of it. Today. Volunteers get a cape and a plant. The plant is soggy.
The plant gathering expedition has reached the far edge of the map. They found one strawberry. They are coming back for a bag.
Lovely ruin, two valleys over, previous owner {past_fort_fate}. Now under goblin tenancy. Asking price: an army.
Survivor of {past_fort} ({past_fort_years}, no regrets, some regrets) seeks a fort that keeps its drinks near its miners.
Everyone remembers {record} at {record_fort}. The bookkeeper asks you to stop bringing it up while he works the orders.
Historian to explain {record}. Several have tried. One wept. One ordered more. We are now hiring a third.
Will swap stories of {past_fort} for ale. One story per mug. I have {past_fort_years} of stories. You will need a cart.
For any info on the goblins who took {past_fort}. Specifically, are they coming here next? Asking for {pop} friends.
Scouts report {enemy} is still at war with us. They have sent no letter to say so, but we can tell from all the arrows.
{monarch}: we would love a visit. Please bring something other than demands. Love, the fort. P.S. thrones available.
{liaison}, regarding the import agreement. Which one? All of them. We have a filing cabinet labelled 'Much to Share'.
Great Rewind counselling. You did not dream it. The world really did stop and start. Yes, you have to dig it again.
Commemorative plate: 1,981 armor stands, Quakefocus. Comes with its own armor stand, from the original set. Of course it does.
Ngumrash Ensebrab and Laba Cócefevu Iwe of The Crazed Hex are not welcome. Neither is Uslôx Ulutodan. Please check names at the gate.
Couriers to The Plain Fellowship, The Society of Creeds, The Silks of Cremating and The Society of Adoration. Same letter, four bands.
To Oddom Oltartilesh: we know you heard about the 148 thrones. They are not a challenge to the crown. They are an accident.

notices.text: Drinks are kept in the drink stockpile. Dwarves are kept near the drinks. Please keep it that way.
If you are thirsty, drink. This notice was not necessary in any other civilization.
Barrels are for opening. Admiring a barrel does not count as drinking from it.
Miners: a mug weighs less than a pick. Carry both.
Dying of thirst beside a full stockpile is no longer considered a tradition.
Do not climb trees. If already in a tree, do not stay in the tree.
Tree branches are not a waiting room.
Dwarves found up trees will be fetched down and given a stern drink.
The 'Safety' burrow is not to be used for safety until the stairs are reviewed.
If something large is coming up the stairs, the 'Safety' burrow is the wrong direction.
Burrows are named by the Overseer. Names are aspirational.
Refuse goes into the pit. Haulers do not.
Please do not fetch rubbish from the pit while others are throwing rubbish into the pit.
Anything dropped in the garbage pit belongs to the garbage pit.
The pit is not a stockpile. The pit is a decision.
Gem cutters are asked to leave one gem rough. Just one. For the mood.
Moods will request whatever we just ran out of. Plan accordingly.
Children seizing workshops must be accompanied by an adult. The adult may not help.
Please do not tell a moody child to tidy the workshop.
Strange moods must queue for the loom room like everybody else. Possessed weavers first.
Work orders are to be read before they are repeated two thousand times.
The manager reminds you: one means one.
The armor stands are not a maze. Please stop using them as a maze.
Sitting on surplus thrones does not make you a noble. Nobles, please stop checking.
If you see an order repeating, shout 'stop'. It will not stop, but you will feel better.
Smoothing is happening. Smoothing will continue to happen. Please step around it.
Rough walls are under the protection of the Rough Walls Society until they are smoothed.
Smoothers are not to be asked how long the queue is. It makes them sad.
The hospital requires a doctor. Any hospital. Either hospital. All of them.
Patients are asked not to diagnose each other. Still, thank you for trying.
The militia is on duty. The militia is off duty. The militia is one dwarf. Check his face.
Nine militia places remain open. They have been open so long they have their own cobwebs.
The captain asks that you salute him when passing, so he feels like there are more of him.
Do not wake the militia. He's resting from not training.
Production order violation forms are available in triplicate, then again, then again.
The mayor's office is closed. The mayor's office has always been closed. There is no mayor.
The sheriff's office is vacant. Crime is asked to wait.
Applications for the hammerer post can be dropped in the empty hammerer's slot.
The dungeon master post remains open. So does the dungeon. Please do not wander in.
Champion wanted. Must be champion of something. Anything. Stair-sitting counts.
Walk through the mist ring slowly to receive your happy thought.
The pumps are for mist. The mist is for joy. The joy is for productivity. Pump.
The windmill is not a ride.
The cistern is full. You may drink from it. That is what it is for. Hello.
Catacomb visitors are asked to speak softly; the residents are light sleepers.
The execution tower is closed for the season. It has a lot of seasons.
Guests are reminded the Overseer's eye may follow them. Smile. It likes merchants.
Animal people visitors may sit at any table. Please do not ask them which animal.
Plant gathering continues in all weather, across all of the map, at all hours.
The far side of the map is still part of the plant-gathering area. So is the near side.
If the gods blink, finish your sentence. You may have to say it again anyway.
Work lost in the Great Rewind must be redone. Moods lost in the Great Rewind may return.
Do not ask whether something happened before or after the gods blinked. It upsets the clerks.
Ghosts of previous forts are to haunt the old fort, not the dining hall.
The ghost by the barrels is not a decoration. It is a reminder. Drink.
Do not invite goblins inside. Goblins invite themselves.
The liaison's caravan is here. Please do not agree to anything before lunch.
Import agreements are not signed in the tavern. Not anymore.
When the liaison says 'there is much to share', hold your purse.
The diplomat is here. Please put the axes behind your back. No, both of them.
Visiting elves: the furniture is stone. The thrones, however, are wood. Do not look in that room.
The fort is at peace with sixteen groups. Please be nice to all sixteen. The other two, less so.
Refugees are welcome. Please give them a bed, a mug and space to stop running.
If a goblin army arrives, the drawbridge will be raised. Please be inside before that. Ideally.
Do not lose any more artifacts. The last one has forty-eight owners.
There are {drinks} drinks in this fort. There is no excuse.
With {drinks} drinks left, please drink slowly and complain quietly.
All {pop} citizens are reminded where the barrels are.
{stone} stones lie loose about the fort. Nobody is to build an armor stand out of them.
Only {wood} logs remain. No more thrones. We mean it this time.
{dogs} dogs is plenty. Please stop bringing in dogs. The dogs agree.
The {cats} cats are not to be counted as militia, however brave they look.
The {farms} farm plots are tilled. Meat is not grown in them. Stop asking.
There is no meat. There is a mushroom shaped like meat. Be grateful.
{gems} gems in stock. One of them must remain rough. Gem cutters, look away.
In memory of {deadname}. Please drink a mug for them. A whole one.
{moodname} has taken a workshop. Whatever they ask for, we just ran out of it.
Congratulations to {masterwright} on {masterwork}. Do not let the Overseer order 2,000 more.
{promoted} is now {post}. The office remains without a chair.
{mineral} has been struck. The Overseer has not yet ordered anything silly from it. Yet.
New migrants: welcome. The barrels are that way. Please, actually, go that way.
A caravan has arrived. The liaison is about to recommend something.
Snow on the map. Plant gathering continues regardless, by order.
Rain all day. The Overseer has dispatched thirty dwarves to collect wet plants.
Clear skies. Gatherers to the far edge of the map, please. Again.
Spring has come. The smoothing queue has been refreshed for the year.
Summer heat. Miners are reminded that thirst is a choice. Drink.
Autumn. Harvest is in. Count the plants twice; the Overseer counts them once.
Winter. Goblin armies prefer this season. So does the cold. Wrap up and lock up.
{pop} dwarves, one tavern. Please take turns being merry.
Only {pop} of us. Please do not die of anything silly.
Year {year}. Another fort, another chance not to repeat {past_fort}.
Dwarves from {past_fort}: you are not in {past_fort} now. You may relax. Slightly.
{past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. Let us all try very hard not to do that.
{past_fort} lasted {past_fort_years}. The betting pool for this fort is in the tavern.
Do not mention {record}. The bookkeeper is still not over it.
{record_fort} gave us {record}. This fort will not. This is a promise from management.
The fort is at war with {enemy}. Please do not leave gifts for them at the gate.
{enemy_race} are not to be admitted as guests, however polite their letter.
Long live {monarch}, who has not visited and is not expected to.
{liaison} is in the depot. Hide the rings.
All citizens of {civ}: drink, dig, and do not smooth anything without a form.
Welcome to {fort}, in {world}. Previous forts in {world} available on request, with sorrow.
Searabbeys veterans are reminded that meat now exists and is not a rumour.
No more than 1,981 armor stands per fort. This rule was written after Quakefocus.
Bomrek Enshalcatten is remembered at every barrel. Please drink one for him.
The Crazed Hex is NOT welcome. Padtufted, Pulledrained and Ironcrowds send their regards.
The Nuanced Hamlet is still at Searabbeys. No, nobody is going to fetch it.
When Iden Loloklolor says 'there is much to share', he means rings. At 210%.
Claspedserpent remains at Quakefocus. It is a silver mace. It does not want to be visited.

ears.text: Every gem cut but this one

help_wanted.text: DRINK CARRIER: Walk beside a miner all day holding a mug. When he looks thirsty, hand it over. When he looks fine, hand it over anyway. Lifesaving work.
WANTED: Tree Spotter. Stand under every tree on the map and shout 'GET DOWN' at any dwarf above you. Must have a loud voice and no interest in climbing.
STAIR LISTENER: Sit at the top of the deep stairs and listen for anything large coming up. Report at once. Do not go down to check. Never go down to check.
PIT ATTENDANT: Stand at the edge of the garbage pit and stop haulers going in after the rubbish. Job requires firmness, a whistle and one long stick.
ORDER READER: Read every work order aloud before it runs. If the number has more than two digits, scream. Previous forts would have loved you.
FURNITURE SHEPHERD: Herd surplus armor stands into a single room and keep them there. They do not move, but it feels like they do at night.
THRONE TESTER: Sit on each surplus throne for one minute and report. There are a lot of thrones. You will be sitting a long time. Cushion provided.
SMOOTHER, SENIOR: Lead a team of three against a queue of ten thousand jobs. Benefits: job security for life. Several lives. All of them.
ROUGH GEM KEEPER: Hide one rough gem from the gem cutters at all times, for use in the next strange mood. Must be sneaky, patient and good with socks.
MOOD ANTICIPATOR: Guess what the next strange mood will demand and stockpile it in advance. Hint: it will be whatever we just used up. It always is.
CHILDMINDER (WORKSHOP): Supervise children in strange moods. Do not interrupt. Do not help. Do bring snacks. Do not let her name the artifact 'Mum'.
LOOM ROOM BUILDER: Construct a loom room before the next possessed weaver arrives. Previous builder was too late. Weaver was not pleased, then was not anything.
CLOTH COUNTER: Count cloth honestly so seven scraps never again pass for a stockpile. Must be able to tell a scrap from a bolt at fifty paces.
DOCTOR, ANY: Four hospitals, some with nobody in them but patients. Any medical experience welcome. Holding a splint the right way up counts.
CHIEF MEDICAL DWARF: The post is vacant. The previous holder vacated it. The one before that also vacated it. Apply in person at the empty hospital.
MILITIA, NINE PLACES: Join the captain, who is lonely, on a squad that is permanently 'Off duty'. Training not scheduled. Napping scheduled frequently.
SQUAD MORALE OFFICER: Keep the militia of one cheerful. Tasks: laughing at his jokes, saluting, being the other nine members when he counts.
MAYOR'S CLERK: Stamp production order violation forms. All day. Every day. Any name will do; the mayor finds the names later. Ink allowance generous.
VIOLATION DEFENDER: Represent dwarves accused of not making the mandated mugs. Cases are lost. Fees are paid in mugs, which is a whole other issue.
SHERIFF: Fort lacks one. Crime has noticed. Duties include standing in a hallway looking official. Badge, desk, no backup, no idea what to do.
HAMMERER: Post vacant. Duties are what they sound like. Applicants who flinch at the word 'hammer' need not apply. Nobody has applied.
DUNGEON MASTER: Fort has a dungeon. Fort lacks a master. Dungeon is getting ideas. Please apply before the dungeon appoints itself.
CHAMPION: Fort requires one. No champion has stepped forward. Wrestling skill optional. Willingness to be called 'Champion' at dinner required.
PUMP OPERATOR, MIST RING: Pump water through a ring of sprayers so passing dwarves feel happy. You will not feel happy. You will feel strong.
WINDMILL GREASER: Climb the windmill weekly and grease the sails. Fall risk moderate. Wind risk high. Tree proximity: thankfully none.
CISTERN GUIDE: Lead thirsty dwarves to the cistern and show them it contains water, which is drinkable. Repeat as needed, which is very often.
CATACOMB USHER: Seat new arrivals in the catacombs. Keep the ghosts calm. Do not seat anyone who is still breathing, no matter how tired they look.
EXECUTION TOWER CARETAKER: Keep the stairs swept and the view nice. Answer visitor questions with 'it's mostly decorative'. Lie convincingly.
GUEST SHADOW: Follow merchants, diplomats and elves around the fort the way the Overseer's eye does, but with snacks. Must walk quietly.
PLANT GATHERER, MAP-WIDE: Collect every plant on the entire map, in any weather. Must own boots, a bag and no sense of 'enough'. Rain is not an excuse.
REWIND CLERK: After the gods blink, record what has to be done again. You will write the same list twice. Sometimes three times. Pens provided twice.
GHOST RELOCATOR: Escort ghosts of previous forts back to their own ruins. They will want a drink first. Give them one. They earned it, late.
GATE GREETER (REFUGEES): Welcome bands fleeing goblin armies. Duties: hot mugs, kind words, counting how many and whether anything is following them.
WAR MAP PAINTER: Repaint the map each season to show goblin armies. Mostly in red. Bulk red paint supplied. Do not lick the brush.
SCOUT, CROOKED HORROR: Confirm the giant beast is still far away. Do it from very far away. Report the answer 'still far' weekly. Lie if necessary.
ARTIFACT CLAIMS ADJUDICATOR: Rule on which of the forty-eight claimants owns the lost greaves. Must be fair. Must have a fast horse. Must not be greaves.
IMPORT AGREEMENT READER: Read every agreement the liaison recommends. Highlight the rings. Mention the percentage. Faint quietly afterwards.
DIPLOMATIC TASTER: Taste every gift basket before it goes to sixteen peaceful neighbours. Taste the goblin baskets too. They are rocks. Gently.
RUIN SURVEYOR: Sketch our old fort from a safe hill and report on its current goblin tenants. Do not knock. Do not leave a forwarding address.
FIRST FLOOR ARCHITECT: Design burrows near the surface, near the drinks and near the exits. Radical concept. Previous architects preferred 'deep'.
WANTED: {past_fort} Veteran. Advise our managers on everything that went wrong in {past_fort_years}. Expect to talk a lot. Expect a tissue.
HISTORIAN: Write the definitive account of how {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. Must be honest. Must not cry on the slab. Slabs are expensive.
RECORD KEEPER: Make sure {fort} never matches {record}. Watch the work orders. Check them again. If you see a fourth digit, pull the lever.
ENVOY TO {monarch}: Explain to the monarch, in person, why the fort has so many thrones. Bring a map, a calm voice and maybe a gift throne.
LIAISON HANDLER: Distract {liaison} during the caravan visit so nobody signs an import agreement by accident. Must know a lot about rings.
ENEMY WATCHER: Keep an eye out for {enemy}. Wave if you see them. No, not that sort of wave. The panicking sort. Yes. That one.
THIRST AUDITOR: Fort holds {drinks} drinks. Find out why anyone is still thirsty. Report findings to the Bureau of Paradox, then drink one.
BREWER, URGENT: Only {drinks} drinks remain. Brew anything. Brew fast. Brew before the miners notice, because then they will start dying near it.
STONE REHOMER: {stone} loose stones need homes. Not as armor stands. Not as thrones. Just put them down somewhere quietly. Somewhere far.
LOG GUARD: Only {wood} logs left. Stand by them so no work order turns them into thrones. Must glare well. Axe permitted for ceremony only.
BUTCHER (THEORETICAL): Prepare meat, should any arrive. Current duties: describing meat to children. Training material: one old drawing.
GRIEF COUNSELLOR: For friends of {deadname}. Main message: next time, the mug is right there. Second message: we're sorry. Third: drink.
MIGRANT GUIDE: Show new arrivals the barrels, the beds and the trees they must not climb. Short tour. Very important tour. Repeat it twice.
MOOD SUPPLIER: {moodname} needs something. We do not have it. We never do. Go find it, quickly, before {moodname} starts eyeing the furniture.
DOG WRANGLER: The fort has {dogs} dogs. They need walking, feeding and assigning. They do not need a squad. Do not let the captain recruit them.
CROWD MARSHAL: {pop} dwarves, one dining hall, one doorway. Keep things moving. Bring a whistle and a strong sense of who was first.
GEM CUTTER (RESTRAINED): Cut gems, but not ALL of them. Leave a few rough. Difficult for some cutters. We will be checking your pockets.
SENTINEL ARCHIVIST: Catalogue every edition of the Quakefocus Sentinel, including the famine issues. Must enjoy reading about 1,981 armor stands.
SEARABBEYS SCOUT: Count the goblins of The Torments of Hating now living in our first fort, and see whether The Nuanced Hamlet is still on its pedestal.
CLAIMANT #49: Join forty-eight others claiming The Amusing Duties. Travel to Fieryaged. Argue. Return. Repeat. Greaves not provided.

order_ads.text: WANTED: {n} of '{job}'. Not two thousand. {n}. The manager has checked twice and is checking again with a lantern.
COMMISSION: '{job}', {n} remaining. Please stop at {n}. Any surplus will be stored in the throne room, which is full.
{n} x '{job}'. Order capped by hand after an incident nobody discusses. The cap is a rock. Do not move the rock.
OPEN ORDER: '{job}' ({n} left). Workers who finish early may rest. Workers who keep going will be gently tackled.
'{job}': {n} owed. Material: {material}. Stock checked by a real dwarf, not by counting seven scraps and calling it a pile.
NEEDED: {n} more '{job}'. Drink before starting. Drink during. Drink after. This order will not be fulfilled by a ghost.
THE MANAGER'S OFFICE seeks a dwarf for '{job}', {n} remaining. Applicants found up trees will not be considered.
'{job}', {n} to go. Workers must not die of thirst at the workshop. There is a barrel. It is two steps away. We measured.
{n} of '{job}' in {material}. Signed off by {manager}, who has promised never to type a fourth digit again.
{manager} requests {n} '{job}'. {manager} also requests that nobody repeat the request. It repeats itself.
REMINDER: '{job}' x{n}. Any dwarf making more than {n} will be asked to explain it to the armor stands.
'{job}': {n} left. This is a real order, not a runaway. We think. Please report any thrones appearing unexpectedly.
{fort} commissions {n} of '{job}'. Material: {material}. The mayor will file a violation if late, and probably if early.
SEASONAL ORDER ({season}): {n} '{job}'. Due before the next blink of the gods, or twice if one happens.
'{job}' ({n} remaining). Mood-proof: if a strange mood steals your workshop, the order waits. Politely. Sulkily.
CALLING ALL CRAFTSDWARVES: {n} '{job}'. Smoothers need not apply; you have ten thousand jobs already, and we see you.
'{job}', {n} outstanding. If the order is not done by spring, the mayor's office will declare it a violation and itself a winner.
{n} more '{job}', please. Material {material}. If we have run out of {material}, a mood will want it. Hide some first.
PLEASE MAKE {n} '{job}'. Then stop. Then go have a drink. Then come back and check you stopped.
'{job}' x{n}. Do not gather plants across the map for this order. Not every order is a plant order. This one is not.
JOB BOARD: '{job}', {n} open. Hazard pay for any dwarf who must walk past the garbage pit. Do not go into the garbage pit.
{n} '{job}' still owed. Previous attempts lost in a Great Rewind. Please do them again, with feeling.
'{job}': {n} to make. Militia members are excused. That is, the captain is excused. He has been excused for years.
NEEDED URGENTLY: {n} '{job}'. Not 'urgently' like the smoothing. Urgently like a real thing that is actually needed.
'{job}' x{n} for the stockpile. The stockpile is already full of armor stands, so please stack carefully on top.
{n} '{job}' in {material}. Workers may not die of thirst next to the {material}. {material} is not drinkable. We asked.
COMMISSION: {n} '{job}', delivered to the depot for {liaison}, who says there is much to share. Mostly our goods.
'{job}' x{n}, by order of {manager}, as a gift for {monarch}. If the monarch does not want them, they go in the throne room.
{n} of '{job}' for the war against {enemy}. Make them sturdy. Make them fast. Make them before the arrows do.
'{job}' ({n} left). Let us not do what {past_fort} did. We all know what {past_fort} did. Nobody wants that again.
{n} '{job}' requested. For comparison, {record_fort} once made {record}. This is a much smaller order. Keep it small.
WORK ORDER '{job}': {n} remaining. If this ever reaches {record}, the manager will be relieved of duty and of quills.
{n} x '{job}'. Previous record of {record} at {record_fort} will not be challenged. This is not a competition. Stop.
'{job}': {n} still needed. Delivered by hand, not by minecart, not by tree branch, not by refuse pit. By hand.
{manager} wants {n} '{job}' from {material}. {manager} has also filed {n} reminders, which are not part of the order.
ORDER NO. {n}: '{job}'. That is the count, not the number of the order. We know. It confuses the clerks too.
'{job}', {n} owed. Perfect job for a dwarf in a strange mood who wants something to do while we find the rough gem.
{n} '{job}' needed for the hospital, which needs a doctor more, but we're starting with what's on the list.
'{job}' x{n}. Contact {manager}. If {manager} is not in, the office is 'Off duty', like the militia. Try again Tuesday.
{n} '{job}' wanted. Please don't let the Overseer see this one. It might get excited and add three zeroes.
{n} '{job}'. Material: {material}. Quakefocus made 1,981 armor stands from a smaller order. We have read the files. Count carefully.
'{job}' x{n}. If this order produces 148 of anything, the manager will be sent to Quakefocus to sit on each throne personally.
{n} '{job}' for the depot. Iden Loloklolor will recommend an import agreement either way. He can wait. He likes waiting.
'{job}' ({n} left). Bomrek of Searabbeys died beside 1,994 drinks. Have a drink before you start. That is not optional.
{n} '{job}' to be finished before The Destined Wickedness arrives. They have not said when. They never say when.

recruit_ads.text: JOIN {squad}! {n} places, all empty, all waiting. The captain has set out chairs for each one and talks to them kindly.
{squad} has {n} openings and one member. That member is {captain}. {captain} would love company. {captain} is begging.
ENLIST IN {squad}. Routine: {routine}. Duty status: 'Off duty'. Duty status since founding: 'Off duty'. Steady work.
{squad} SEEKS {n} BRAVE DWARVES. Or any dwarves. Or a dog. The captain is not fussy. The dog has already been asked.
A MILITIA OF ONE IS A LONELY MILITIA. {squad} has {n} spaces. {captain} has drawn faces on the empty helmets.
{squad}: {members} strong, {n} short. Total kills: {kills}. Total naps: many more. Join for the naps. Stay for the naps.
{captain} OF {squad} WANTS YOU. And you. And you. And seven more of you. Recruitment drive ongoing since the last fort.
{squad} is recruiting. Applicants must be able to stand, hold a weapon and not go to the 'Safety' burrow when told to.
JOIN {squad} and defend {fort} from whatever comes up the stairs. Last time, nobody was there to stop it. Be the somebody.
{squad} ({members} members) needs {n} more before the goblins notice. The goblins have noticed. Please hurry.
PROTECT THE BARRELS. {squad} guards the drink stockpile, the one place nobody seems to visit. {n} spots open.
{squad}: no experience needed, no training given. Routine is '{routine}', which {captain} interprets very loosely.
{squad} OFFERS: a uniform, a spear, a bunk, and the gratitude of {captain}, who is tired of being the whole army.
WANTED FOR {squad}: {n} dwarves who can tell the difference between a goblin army and a merchant caravan. Mostly by the spears.
{squad} has {kills} kills and {members} members. Statistically, that is a lot of kills each. Join and lower the average.
THE FORT NEEDS YOU. {squad} has {n} vacancies and a captain who has started training with the armor stands.
{squad} is the only thing between {fort} and the next goblin army. {squad} is currently {members} dwarf. Do the maths.
JOIN {squad}, the militia that never fails, because it never goes out. {n} places open. Comfortable chairs guaranteed.
{captain} seeks {n} recruits for {squad}. Must not climb trees on patrol. Must drink before patrol. Must do a patrol.
{squad}: {n} openings. Duties: standing at the gate looking fierce while refugees come in and goblins don't.
ENLIST TODAY in {squad} and receive one free mug, one free spear and one free strongly worded talk about the stairs.
{squad} recruitment fair this week. {captain} will be there. {captain} will be the only one there. Please come.
{squad} needs {n} more if the fort is to stop being defended by one dwarf and a goose. The goose is not officially enlisted.
NO MORE 'SAFETY' BURROWS. Join {squad} and stand at the top of the stairs instead. {n} positions, all upstairs.
{squad} WANTS YOU to stand bravely between {enemy} and the dining hall. {n} places open. Bring an appetite and armour.
{enemy} has an army. {squad} has {members}. Help even the odds. {n} vacancies. Spears in the hall, courage in the tavern.
REMEMBER {past_fort}. {squad} does. {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. {squad} has {n} openings so it doesn't happen here.
{squad} defends {fort} in the name of {monarch} and {civ}. The monarch is not aware of this. {n} places still open.
{squad}: armour available in quantity. Seriously, there are a lot of armor stands. Some even have armour. {n} spots.
{squad} is training! Today's routine: '{routine}'. Tomorrow: probably '{routine}' again. Consistency wins wars.
{squad} has {n} vacancies and 1,981 armor stands' worth of empty kit inherited from Quakefocus. Choose any. Choose all.
JOIN {squad}. The Destined Wickedness has an army. The High Cruelties have another. {squad} has {members}. Help.
{squad} still remembers the Safety burrow at Creaturemirrored. {n} openings, so nobody hides thirty levels down again.
{squad} recruits in honour of Searabbeys, taken by The Torments of Hating. {n} places. One day we march back.
{squad} needs {n} dwarves before The Crazed Hex does to us what it did to Padtufted. Twice, counting the Vice of Fins.

vacancy_ads.text: POSITION VACANT: {post}. Office, desk, chair. No applicant. The last one left a note: 'paperwork'.
{post} WANTED. Must not die of thirst at the desk. The desk is near a barrel for this very reason.
{fort} seeks a {post}. The post has been empty so long it has started filing its own production order violations.
APPLY NOW: {post}. Duties include duties. Perks include a chair nobody else will sit on, because it is yours.
{post}: vacant, again. Like the mayor, sheriff, hammerer, dungeon master and champion. It is a quiet corridor.
THE FORT NEEDS A {post}. The fort also needs a doctor, a sheriff and nine soldiers, but one thing at a time.
{post} required. Training given by nobody, because nobody has ever done it here. You'll be the expert at once.
{post}: the office is smoothed, which is more than can be said for most rooms. Smooth office, rough job.
OPENING: {post}. Previous {post} left for a 'Safety' burrow and did not come back up. The office is fine. Mostly.
{post} needed urgently. The Overseer has appointed nobody. The Overseer has appointed many armor stands, however.
VACANCY: {post}. No interview. No experience. No competition. A dwarf could get this job just by walking past.
{post}, {fort}. Apply in person, in a whisper, before the mayor files a violation against you for applying.
WANTED: {post}. The badge is polished. The chair is warm, from the last dwarf who sat in it to read this advert.
{post} VACANT. We have tried asking the cats. The cats refused. The cats refuse everything. You are our next hope.
{post} needed. Must accept a title, answer to it at dinner and not hide when called.
{fort} has {post}-shaped hole. Plug it. Benefits: a nicer bedroom someday, complaints always.
THE {post} OFFICE IS OPEN. It has always been open. The door was never shut because nobody was there to shut it.
{post}: one opening. Previous holder is a ghost now and still turns up for work. Please be nice. Share the desk.
{post} WANTED. The last fort never filled it either. Nor the one before. Break the cycle. Be the {post}.
NO {post}? NO PROBLEM, says the Overseer. Many problems, say the dwarves. Help settle the argument by applying.
SEEKING A {post} for {fort}. Experience with runaway work orders, thirsty miners and missing doctors preferred.
{post} vacancy. The previous {post} of {past_fort} has written in to say 'good luck'. It did not sound sincere.
{post} required. {past_fort} had one for {past_fort_years}. It did not help, but it did look official.
{post}, appointed on behalf of {monarch} of {civ}, who will not notice either way. Apply anyway. For dignity.
VACANT: {post}. The liaison recommends filling it through an import agreement. We recommend a dwarf instead.
{post} needed before {enemy} arrives. They are unlikely to wait for the hiring process. Short interview, then.
{post} VACANT, like every office in Creaturemirrored. Mayor, sheriff, champion: pick one. Pick all.
{post} wanted. Quakefocus had four hospitals and two doctors. Do not let this office become the other two.
{post}: Iden Loloklolor says there is much to share, and recommends an import agreement to fill it.
{post} needed. Oddom Oltartilesh has been told the post is filled. Please fill it before he checks.

real_estate.head: Former 'Safety' Burrow, Very Deep
real_estate.text: Thirty levels down, utterly quiet, with a direct staircase to everywhere, which, as previous tenants discovered, also means everything comes to you.

real_estate.head: Treehouse, One Branch, As Is
real_estate.text: Breathtaking views from a single sturdy branch. No water up here. No ladder either. Previous resident stayed rather longer than planned.

real_estate.head: Room Beside the Drink Stockpile
real_estate.text: Barrels on three sides, which is the only floor plan proven to keep a miner alive. Tenants must drink at least one. Inspections weekly.

real_estate.head: Pit-View Studio
real_estate.text: Overlooks the refuse pit from a safe railing. Watch rubbish go in. Never come out. Tenants who climb down to fetch things forfeit the deposit.

real_estate.head: Armor Stand Showroom, Furnished
real_estate.text: Comes with 400 armor stands, which cannot be removed, sold or burned. Excellent for dwarves who like company that stands very still.

real_estate.head: Throne Room (One of Many)
real_estate.text: Enjoy royal living in one of the fort's many surplus throne rooms. Every chair is a throne. Every guest is a king. Nobles not admitted.

real_estate.head: Unsmoothed Cave, Rare Find
real_estate.text: Original rough walls, never touched by a chisel. A true heritage property. Smoothers circle outside at dusk. Locks provided.

real_estate.head: Smoothing Queue Apartment
real_estate.text: Your room is on the list. It will be smoothed. Eventually. Possibly in your grandchild's lifetime. Live rough meanwhile, and enjoy it.

real_estate.head: Loom Room, Partially Built
real_estate.text: Two walls, half a floor and a weaver standing in the doorway with a faraway look. Finish it quickly. We cannot stress that enough.

real_estate.head: Hospital Ward, No Doctor
real_estate.text: Spacious beds, clean splints, a bucket. The one thing missing is anyone medical. Ideal for patients who prefer to heal on their own.

real_estate.head: Militia Barracks, Ten Beds
real_estate.text: Ten bunks, one occupant. The captain is very tidy and very lonely. Nine spare beds rent by the night. Training not compulsory. Or offered.

real_estate.head: Mayor's Office Annex
real_estate.text: Desk, chair and a mountain of production order violation forms. The mayor is never in. The forms keep arriving anyway, by themselves.

real_estate.head: Vacant Sheriff's Quarters
real_estate.text: Includes a jail cell, a badge on a hook and an empty chair. Crime-free in the sense that nobody is counting. Quiet neighbourhood, for now.

real_estate.head: Mist Ring Cottage
real_estate.text: Wake to a soft spray from the pumps and a happy thought by breakfast. Slight dampness. Very slight beards. Beard-dryer included.

real_estate.head: Windmill Loft
real_estate.text: Breezy, bright and constantly turning. Ideal for dwarves who like their bedroom to rotate. Hats must be tied down. Hats will still leave.

real_estate.head: Cistern-Side Flat
real_estate.text: Fresh water a stone's throw away. Unlike some forts, tenants here are allowed and in fact begged to drink it. Damp walls; dry wit.

real_estate.head: Catacomb Duplex
real_estate.text: Two levels of quiet, roomy living among the honoured dead. Neighbours never complain. Some neighbours float. Rent in candles.

real_estate.head: Execution Tower Penthouse
real_estate.text: Top floor, best view in the fort, short history. Ask the agent about the trapdoor. The agent will change the subject to the view.

real_estate.head: Garden Plot, Far Edge of Map
real_estate.text: Located exactly where the Overseer sends gatherers in the rain. Daily visitors. Damp visitors. Bring a bag; you'll be sent out anyway.

real_estate.head: Guest Suite, Watched
real_estate.text: For visiting merchants and diplomats. The Overseer's eye may drop by and follow you around. Wave nicely. It keeps a polite distance.

real_estate.head: Moody Child's Former Workshop
real_estate.text: Recently vacated by a toddler who produced an artifact here. Crayon on the walls is now legally significant. Do not scrub.

real_estate.head: Gem-Cutter's Den, Every Gem Cut
real_estate.text: Every stone in sight polished to perfection. Not a rough one left. Strange-mood visitors will be very disappointed. Ideal for cutters.

real_estate.head: Ground-Floor Burrow, Near Exit
real_estate.text: A radical new layout: safe room one level down, beside the drinks, with a door you can close. Previous 'Safety' burrows look on jealously.

real_estate.head: Ruin Overlook, Hill Site
real_estate.text: Gorgeous views of a former dwarven fortress, now goblin-occupied. Enjoy the sunsets, the spikes, and the distant shouting. Binoculars extra.

real_estate.head: Refugee Bunkhouse
real_estate.text: Shared rooms for bands fleeing goblin armies. Hot mugs, warm blankets and the reassuring sound of a raised drawbridge. Run-in welcome.

real_estate.head: War Room, Map Included
real_estate.text: Big table, little goblin figures, one map mostly coloured in red. Lease includes access to the fort's entire army, i.e. one dwarf.

real_estate.head: Import Agreement Office
real_estate.text: Perfect for a visiting liaison. Comfy chair, a pile of rings and an echo that repeats 'there is much to share' all night. Unclear why.

real_estate.head: Rewind-Proof Bedroom
real_estate.text: This room has been dug three times due to the Great Rewinds and is now extra solid. May contain duplicate furniture from a blink.

real_estate.head: {past_fort} Heritage Flat
real_estate.text: Faithful replica of a bedroom from {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. Authentic details include one barrel nobody opened. Open it.

real_estate.head: Starter Home, Lessons Included
real_estate.text: Built by veterans of {past_fort}, who lasted {past_fort_years}. Everything they wish they had: drink nearby, no trees, short stairs.

real_estate.head: Record-Setter's Storeroom
real_estate.text: Once held part of {record} at {record_fort}. Fully cleared, aired, and blessed. Faint feeling that something is about to be ordered.

real_estate.head: Royal Guest Room
real_estate.text: Kept ready in case {monarch} ever visits. Nobody has slept here. The bed is offended. Short-term rental while the monarch is far away.

real_estate.head: Liaison's Spare Room
real_estate.text: Where {liaison} stays when the caravan comes. Rented out between visits. Do not sign anything left on the pillow.

real_estate.head: Siege-Safe Hall
real_estate.text: Thick doors, no windows, nowhere for {enemy} to get in. Lovely for dwarves who want to stop thinking about {enemy}. Hard to leave.

real_estate.head: Fort Address, {fort}
real_estate.text: Prime location in {fort}, {pop} neighbours, with {drinks} drinks within walking distance. Please walk the distance. Daily.

real_estate.head: Stone-Built Lodge
real_estate.text: Built from the fort's spare stones and barely a dent in the {stone}-stone pile. Every wall is a monument to things we didn't build.

real_estate.head: Kennel Annex
real_estate.text: Lively, loud and full of {dogs} dogs who love you instantly. No cats. Cats rent across the hall and sneer at the doormat.

real_estate.head: Thirst-Free Suite
real_estate.text: Comes with a barrel that cannot be moved, removed or ignored. Contains drink. Tenants must touch it daily. We have seen what happens.

real_estate.head: Late Tenant's Room
real_estate.text: Formerly the room of {deadname}. Tidy, quiet, a single mug left by the bed, full. Please drink it in their memory, then sweep.

real_estate.head: Migrant Corridor Lots
real_estate.text: Fresh lots along the main corridor, perfect for the newly arrived. Guide included. Guide will point at the barrels until you nod.

real_estate.head: Meatless Cellar
real_estate.text: Spacious, cool, empty. Built for hanging meat. There is no meat. It is a beautiful room for wishing.

real_estate.head: Rainy Season Shack
real_estate.text: Surface shack used by plant gatherers on the map's far edge. Damp, cosy, close to every soggy shrub the Overseer wants picked.

real_estate.head: SEARABBEYS, Goblin-Managed, Must See
real_estate.text: Our first fort, now under the firm hand of The Torments of Hating. Upgrades: spikes, cages, a moat of regret. The Nuanced Hamlet possibly included.

real_estate.head: Searabbeys Drink Hall, Fully Stocked
real_estate.text: Still holds roughly 2,000 drinks, untouched since the meatless years. Goblin landlords drink most of it now. Ghost of a thirsty miner stays.

real_estate.head: Quakefocus Armor Stand Surplus Lot
real_estate.text: Field of 1,981 armor stands, sold by the acre. Ideal for scarecrows, forests of stands or a very quiet army. Buyer collects. Buyer weeps.

real_estate.head: Quakefocus Throne Gallery
real_estate.text: Forty-eight of the 148 surplus thrones, arranged in rows. Sit in any. Rule over nothing. Elves strongly advised not to visit.

real_estate.head: Quakefocus Hospital, Two Wings
real_estate.text: Two of the old fort's four hospitals, both doctorless since founding. Beds, buckets and the echo of nobody coming. Healing optional.

real_estate.head: Creaturemirrored Branch, Historic
real_estate.text: The single most famous tree branch in the world. Viewable from the ground only. Not for sale. Do not climb. Stop asking to climb.

real_estate.head: Jackaldefense Townhouse
real_estate.text: Lovely human-occupied townhouse, recently The Distinct Dungeon's. The Grooved Council is the landlord. Their lease says 'forever'.

real_estate.head: Shadyghosts Cabin
real_estate.text: Rustic cabin near Omo Fewethauyira's hunting grounds. Very cheap. Very quiet. Very sudden. Agent will not come within a mile.
